summary: Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and under August Wilhelm von Schlegel at the University of Bonn (Ph.D. 1827). He served at Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and full professor (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard Divinity School, and Columbia University (Ph.D. ~2003). He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and directed the University of Washington's South Asia Center (2007).

Christian Lindtner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Copenhagen by 1982. He also served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Magister and Ph.D. at the University of Vienna, later working as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2012) and senior lecturer at SOAS (2014).
Christian Mabel Duff was an Indology scholar who studied at Kiel University under Paul Deussen from circa 1892 to 1896.

Christian Matthias Boehm works in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied under Toshifumi Konno, earned degrees from SOAS, TUM, Imperial College London, and Cambridge, and held posts at the Max Planck Institute (2017–2018) and the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (2019).

Christian Schweigaard Stang was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Oslo under Sten Konow and Antoine Meillet, later serving at Oslo as an associate professor (1930) and professor of Slavic philology (1938–1970).

Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields. A student of Seizan Yanagida, he worked as an associate researcher at the Chunghwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (1998–2001) and as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2012).

Christian von Ehrenfels was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Graz. He held a post at the University of Vienna (~1888–1896) and served as professor of philosophy at the German University in Prague (~1896–1929).

Christian-Friedrich von Graefe was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the Saint Petersburg Theological Academy (1810) and Main Pedagogical Institute, and served as conservator (1821) and honorary director (1840) of the State Hermitage Museum.

Christiane Papa-Kalantari is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She worked as a research fellow at the University of Vienna (2003–2006) and became a postdoctoral researcher and project director at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2025).

Christiane Strothmann works in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts as Artist in Progress (2016–2018) and lecturer (2024–2026) at Folkwang University of the Arts, and as a lecturer at the University of Paderborn (2023–2026).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University under Pieter Jacob Cosijn and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He was professor of Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She completed a doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).
Christine Henriëtte Raabe was an Indologist. She studied at Utrecht University under Johan Hendrik Gallée and doctoral supervisor Willem Caland, completing her Ph.D. in 1911.

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She worked as a researcher (1989–1995) and director of research (attested 2014) at the CNRS.

Christmas Humphreys was a scholar and practitioner in Buddhist studies and religious studies who was educated at Malvern College and Trinity Hall. He founded the Buddhist Society in 1924 and served as its president until 1983.

Christoph Anderl works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna and completed his Ph.D. under Christoph Harbsmeier at the University of Oslo in 2004, later joining Ghent University as a permanent member (~2012).

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg under Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan, Albrecht Wezler, and Lambert Schmithausen, and served as director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (~1994–2013).

Christoph Emmrich specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned Dr. Phil. degrees from Free University of Berlin, University of Tübingen, and Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels, and was appointed assistant professor at the University of Toronto in 2006.
